signals.description: Es soll eine IT-Anwendung zur Digitalisierung der Vorgänge in Bezug auf die Trichinenuntersuchung, das Management von Monitoring-Proben im Tiergesundheitsbereich und das Management im Falle eines Ausbruches der Afrikanischen Schweinepest (ASP) als SaaS-Cloud-Lösung beschafft werden. Die IT-Anwendung muss kompatibel zur Jagdstatistik-Anwendung der Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH sein. Mit dieser werden im Freistaat Thüringen die Streckendaten (Daten der von Jägern erlegten Wildtiere) erfasst. Die IT-Anwendung soll sowohl als Web- (nutzbar in den gängigen Browsern) als auch Mobile App-Anwendung (Betriebssysteme iOS und Android) zur Verfügung stehen. Als App wird im Rahmen der Ausschreibung eine Anwendung definiert, die vor Verwendung durch den Nutzer auf einem mobilen Gerät installiert werden muss und auch nur dort genutzt werden kann. In der Regel erfolgt dies auf einem Smartphone oder Tablet mithilfe eines sogenannten App-Stores. Es wird zwei wesentliche Nutzergruppen geben: a) Verwaltungs- bzw. Labormitarbeiter b) verwaltungsexterne Nutzer (z. B. Jagdausübungsberechtigte) Die verwaltungsexternen Nutzer erfassen Daten zu erlegten bzw. geschlachteten Tieren. Erforderlichenfalls stellen diese zudem Anträge zur Untersuchung dieser Tiere auf Trichinen und/oder bestimmte Wildtierseuchen bei den zuständigen Behörden bzw. der zuständigen Untersuchungseinrichtung des Freistaates Thüringen. Die Untersuchungsergebnisse sollen über die IT-Anwendung abrufbar sein. Die zuständigen Behörden (Veterinär- und Lebensmittelüberwachungsämter der Landkreise und kreisfreie Städte - Veterinärbehörden) betreiben die Trichinenuntersuchungslabore. Diese sollen über eine eigene Nutzeroberfläche auf die durch die externen Nutzer in der IT-Anwendung erfassten Antragsdaten zugreifen und die Untersuchungsergebnisse an die Antragssteller zurück übermitteln können. Zudem soll für die zuständigen Behörden eine Laborsoftware zur Verfügung gestellt werden, mit Hilfe dieser auf Basis der Antragsdaten die Untersuchungstätigkeiten dokumentiert werden können. Im Falle der Monitoring-Proben im Tiergesundheitsbereich ist das Labor des Auftraggebers im Thüringer Landesamt für Verbraucherschutz die zuständige Untersuchungseinrichtung. Die dort in Nutzung befindliche Laborsoftware (LIMS) soll über die HIT-Datenbank auf die von den Nutzern eingegebenen Informationen zu den Proben zugreifen können. Die IT-Anwendung muss daher über eine Schnittstelle zur HIT-Datenbank verfügen. Eine direkte Verbindung zum LIMS ist nicht vorgesehen. Die IT-Anwendung soll den Verwaltungsmitarbeitenden zur Abbildung verwaltungsinterner Vorgänge sowie betroffenen Nutzern außerhalb der Verwaltung zur Datenerfassung und Antragsstellung gegenüber sowie dem Empfang von Bescheiden von den zuständigen Behörden zur Verfügung stehen. Während die Anwendungsfälle Trichinenuntersuchung, Management von Monitoring-Proben im Tiergesundheitsbereich sowie die Schnittstelle zur Jagdstatistikanwendung dauerhaft zur Verfügung stehen sollen, soll der Anwendungsfall des Managements im Falle eines Ausbruches der Afrikanischen Schweinepest (ASP) nur anlassbezogen nutz- und verfügbar sein. Darüber hinaus soll auch eine Einführungsunterstützung sowie Schulung der Mitarbeitenden der zuständigen Behörden im Angebot als initiale Leistung enthalten sein. Vertragsschluss erfolgt über einen EVB-IT Cloud-Vertrag. Die Beschaffung erfolgt durch den Auftraggeber zur Nutzung durch alle Landkreise und kreisfreien Städte in Thüringen. Die Verwendung der IT-Anwendung für die vorgenannten Zwecke ist für die Landkreisen und kreisfreien Städten verpflichtend. Den Jägern ist die Verwendung dagegen freigestellt. Das bedeutet, diese können von der Verwendung der IT-Anwendung absehen. Das bisherige analoge System zur Probenahme wird vorerst parallel weitergeführt. Die 21 Veterinär- und Lebensmittelüberwachungsämter der 22 Landkreise und kreisfreien Städte im Freistaat Thüringen sind unter anderem zuständig für die Entgegennahme und Untersuchung von Proben geschlachteter oder erlegter Tiere, die für den Verzehr durch den Menschen vorgesehen sind, auf Trichinella spp. Darüber hinaus bestehen Zuständigkeiten im Hinblick auf die Erlaubniserteilung zur Entnahme von Proben, die zur Untersuchung auf Trichinen vorgesehen sind, durch verwaltungsexterne Personen. Den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern, die die vorgenannten Verwaltungsleistungen in Anspruch nehmen möchten, soll ermöglicht werden, die erforderlichen Antragsdaten nach den Grundsätzen des Online-Zugangsgesetzes (OZG) digital zu erfassen, den Antrag papierlos dem jeweils zuständigen Veterinär- und Lebensmittelüberwachungsamt zu übermitteln und die Bescheide der zuständigen Behörden zu empfangen. Zudem soll die Möglichkeit geschaffen werden, weiteren Berichtspflichten (z. B. die Erfassung der Jagdstrecken durch Jägerinnen und Jäger) in digitaler Form nachzukommen. Die Untersuchung von Wildschweinen auf Trichinella spp. erfolgt nur dann, wenn das Tier zu einem Lebensmittel werden soll. Dies führt nach den bisherigen Erfahrungen pro Jahr zur Untersuchung von bis zu 30.000 Stück Schwarzwild in Thüringen. Diese Zahlen schwanken. Darüber hinaus sind die Behörden der Veterinärüberwachung für die Umsetzung eines regelmäßigen Monitorings von erlegten Wildtieren auf bestimmte Tierseuchenerreger verantwortlich. In Abhängigkeit vom aktuellen tierseuchenrechtlichen Status variiert die Probenzahl voraussichtlich zwischen ca. 5.000 und 30.000 Proben im Jahr. Die Datenerfassung und Antragsstellung sowie der Empfang der Bescheide sollen hier ebenso für die jeweils betroffenen Bürgerinnen und Bürger ermöglicht werden. Die erfassten Daten sollen über die Anwendung an das für die Untersuchung der Proben zuständige Landesamt für Verbraucherschutz übermittelt werden. Der Anwendungsteil für das Management von ASP-Ausbrüchen soll sich bedientechnisch an den vorgenannten Anwendungsteilen (insb. dem Monitoring von erlegten Wildtieren auf bestimmte Tierseuchenerreger) orientieren und inhaltlich mit diesen gemäß den fachlichen Anforderungen interagieren. Dieser Anwendungsteil soll anlassbezogen je betroffener Behörde (Veterinärbehörden der Landkreise und kreisfreien Städte und gegebenenfalls der Auftraggeber) aktivierbar sein. Eine Verwendung soll neben einem Ausbruch der ASP in Thüringen auch im Rahmen von Übungen zur Vorbereitung auf den Ausbruchsfall erfolgen. Ein letzter Anwendungsteil umfasst die Erfassung und Meldung der Jagdstrecken durch die Jägerinnen und Jäger. Diese Meldung umfasst alle jagdbaren Tierarten. Für diese Dokumentationspflicht sollen sich die Erlegedaten aus den vorgenannten Anwendungsteilen nachnutzen, aber auch neue Erlegedaten erfassen lassen können. Für den erforderlichen Datenaustausch mit der Jagdstatistik-Anwendung der Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH ist eine entsprechende Schnittstelle vorzusehen. Die Jägerinnen und Jäger haben bereits direkten Zugriff auf die Jagdstatistik-Anwendung. Die Schnittstelle soll es ihnen ermöglichen, aus der IT-Anwendung heraus Zugriff zu nehmen und so die Meldung durch Datenübernahme zu erleichtern. Die Anwendung soll für die Nutzung durch Verwaltungspersonal im Freistaat Thüringen sowie die jeweils betroffenen Bürgerinnen und Bürger im Freistaat Thüringen bereitgestellt werden. Dadurch müssen die Lizenz- und Nutzungsbedingungen eine Nutzung durch Beschäftigte des Landes, der Kommunen und durch verwaltungsexterne Personen ermöglichen. Die Anzahl der künftigen Nutzer kann derzeit nicht genau beziffert werden, da die Nutzung der IT-Anwendung den Jägerinnen und Jägern freigestellt ist. Jedoch kann die Zahl der Jägerinnen und Jäger in Thüringen ein Anhaltspunkt sein, sie beläuft sich auf ca. 13.000. Hinzu kommen ca. 100 Verwaltungsmitarbeiterinnen und -mitarbeiter.

signals.description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.

signals.description: THIS IS A RETENDER TO OCID ocds-h6vhtk-058a17 Carmarthenshire County Council Healthy Communities & Public Protection Service are looking to procure an EPOS system that is multifunctional and can operate across several facilities. The system should be able to manage both catering and retail operations as well as having the capability to offer additional functionality detailed in the specification below, to help facilities manage their daily financial transactions with a key driver being to reduce costs, drive sales and deliver better customer service. The EPOS system will be installed in cafés and restaurants within leisure-based facilities such as leisure centres, country parks, small hotel, museums, art venues and theatres. The system will be expected to help facilitate the daily operation of such venues to varying degrees, the capability to tailor the system set up based on a venues requirement will be an important factor (i.e. some facilities will only require an EPOS to run F&B and retail sales, where another may need to be able to facilitate F&B, Retail, Ticketing and Membership capability etc.). The ability to manage facility admissions, retail sales, daily stock management and provide comprehensive real time back-office management data are just some of the key functionalities expected of the system. signals.description: Network Rail is looking to procure an end-to-end Virtual Accessibility Tours service for a baseline portfolio of 250 designated railway stations across Great Britain. The proposed service would include station surveys, LiDAR scanning, panoramic imagery, creation of accessible interactive virtual tours and supporting digital assets, publication support, testing, accessibility assurance, implementation, training, ongoing support and maintenance, content updates and future re-scanning services. The current delivery assumption is that, following a planned contract award in early February 2027, the first 100 station tours would be delivered, accepted and operational by June 2027, with the remaining 150 completed by October 2027. The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to obtain supplier feedback on the draft requirements, the deliverability of the proposed timetable and the suitability of a fixed-price commercial model where the station composition and sequencing may change. signals.description: This procurement covers the Population Health Management framework. The framework will cover population health management software solutions that enable analysis and management of health data from a variety of sources to improve healthcare delivery and decision-making. This will empower Approved Organisations and stakeholders to deliver proactive, personalised care while improving efficiency and supporting preventative health interventions. Also can support addressing health inequalities and the wider social determinants and support the decision-making process across the health and social care sector. The framework is divided into three lots: Lot 1: Population Health Management Digital Solutions Delivery of population health management systems that will support the NHS's and other public sector organisations desire to deliver population level health and care across whole, or large-scale areas of the population - for example, an integrated care system, a city or town, a health community, a large acute Trust or a local authority - or multiples of these. Lot 1 is suitable for solutions with the below characteristics: • Solutions that can address large scale populations, however defined. • Multiple features and functionality, covering a wide range of Population Health Management. • Typically draws data from a range of sources of other organisations. • Horizontal integration to provide large populations to manage. • May or may not include the features and functionality of more specialist solutions. Lot 2: Consultancy &Support Services The nature of services will be to address a variety of needs through providing information, advice, direction and potential solutions to customers. Suppliers will be expected to be able to assist customers to make more informed decisions surrounding their population health programme. • Support of the delivery of population health management to the NHS and broader public sector. • Consultancy services are about helping the NHS or other public sector organisations that may use this framework to implement and deliver population support for some or all of the people who live in the areas they either commission or provide health and care services to. • Consultancy could extend across the NHS, wider health, public health, local government, broader policy areas impacting on health (such as transportation policy, housing policy, employment, environmental - other areas of policy relating to population health management and social determinants of health. • Consultancy might also be more targeted, dealing with a more limited area of healthcare, such as risk stratification, social prescribing, medicines usage, etc. Lot 3: Combined Solutions This Lot covers the provision of Population Health Management solutions that deliver bundle services or comprehensive workflows. Population Health Management provided under this Lot should ensure a seamless, integrated approach, delivering all the necessary components required for Approved Organisations. Across all lots, suppliers must provide: • Software licences or subscriptions • Implementation, configuration, and integration services • Training, onboarding, and change management support • Ongoing maintenance, updates, and technical support • Clear service level agreements and performance reporting Lot 1: .

signals.description: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.

signals.description: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS All central government departments and UK public sector bodies can access open banking related tools and services. Description Instead of relying on card payments, open banking services provide citizens and businesses with an alternative method of paying and/or receiving money from the public sector. You will be able to access a range of open banking services including: payment initiation service providers (PISPs): let you pay companies directly from your bank account rather than using your debit or credit card through a third party, such as Visa or Mastercard account information service providers (AISPs): being an authorised AISP means that a company can access an individual’s bank account data from their financial institution with their explicit consent To help you find the services and suppliers to meet your needs you will be able to use the following filters: service type total contract value hosting and delivery capabilities This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) will run for 8 years. Benefits open banking will reduce customer transaction costs where card payments are the existing and only method of payment payments can be made directly from bank account to bank account without the need to repeatedly input details existing customers of the Payment Acceptance framework can transition to Open Banking includes real time bank account data to confirm payee account details reducing the risk of error payments and minimising losses due to fraud Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS Expires: 07/12/2031 How to buy You can access the Open Banking DPS through the Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace. you will need to select the ‘financial services’ section, and scroll to ‘Open Banking’ Select the ‘access as a buyer’ link. you will then be asked to either sign into your Dynamic Purchasing Marketplace account or register for one Accept the terms and conditions of the DPS as a buyer. You can then view and manage your ‘DPS category exports’ page where you will have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export (this is how you filter the suppliers to find those that can meet your needs) When creating a new category use the filtering tool to specify your needs and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘save category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From the ‘manage your category exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (the export is to an Excel spreadsheet). Close the DPS. Use your supplier shortlist to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers in your shortlist to bid against your detailed statement of requirements, evaluation criteria and contract format. Your supplier list is valid for 2 working days from the date of creation. If you do not use your list within 2 working days you will need to create a new supplier list (follow steps 6 to 10). You can use our eSourcing tool to run a competition or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. read guidance for our eSourcing tool Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your needs. You should allow enough time for suppliers to review, prepare a response and ask clarification questions. Evaluate supplier responses. Award the contract. signals.description: Digital Payments & Associated Data Services Summary This framework will give the public sector access to various innovative digital payment and data services. These services include merchant acquiring and gateway services. They also include Bacs, Direct Debit, open banking payments, and account information services. RM6411 is let under the Procurement Act 2023. Description RM6411 Digital Payments & Associated Data Services will replace RM6325 Payment Acceptance 2 . It will provide the public sector with a compliant and cost-effective way to access: transactional payment services advanced financial data services This enables the movement of funds in and out of government. Let under the Procurement Act 2023, this agreement aims to: drive payments and financial data innovation simplify and speed up access to financial solutions and data provide a compliant route to market that offers good value for money open up financial data to provide actionable intelligence. The framework will cover a range of digital payments and associated data services. It focuses on these key areas: digital payment management: handling both incoming and outgoing digital payments high-volume transaction capabilities: facilitating the execution of large-scale, bulk payments enhanced security and data insights: using financial data to: provide operational transparency minimise processing errors reduce fraud Benefits: range of payment methods: buyers can choose familiar options like credit/debit cards and direct debits lower transaction costs : open banking infrastructure allows buyers to bypass some card network fees accelerated fund settlement: improving cash flow through near-real-time fund availability paperless financial data verification: instantly verify a citizen’s income or expenditure advanced identity fraud prevention: using secure, real-time bank account ownership verification frictionless user experience: users can authorise payments using their own banking apps Product types: The agreement plans to deliver a wide range of financial capabilities, including: card processing: enabling the acceptance of credit and debit card payments through: online portals phone systems physical terminals bacs & direct debit payments: access to established “bulk” payment rails, including: direct debit for recurring collections faster payments for near-instant transfers CHAPS (clearing house automated payment system) for high-value, same-day transactions open banking payments: allows citizens to pay using their own banking app open banking data services: provide authorised access to a user’s real-time financial data Customer engagement Engagement sessions started in April 2026. They will continue to run until November 2026. If you would like to speak to us about the proposed agreement, please email: digitalpayments@gcagov.uk . Supplier engagement We held supplier engagement sessions in March, April, May and July 2026. If you wish to join future sessions, contact digitalpayments@gca.gov.uk . Include “RM6411 Digital Payments & Associated Data Services Supplier Engagement” in the subject line. signals.description: ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation offering a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions for the wider public sector. We are establishing a framework to cover the provision document management solutions including digitisation, off-site storage, and confidential shredding of documents. The Framework is divided into 7 lots. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details (including further details on each of the lots) - the closing date for submission of Tenders is 12:00 (12 noon / 12pm) on 12 October 2026. To tender (please proceed to step (e) if an expression of interest has already been completed): (a) Go to https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ (b) Register (if not already registered on ProContract e.g., via https://procontract.due-north.com/Register); (c) Search for tender opportunity 390_27 (via "View Opportunities" from the EastMidsTenders Portal, or alternatively via searching on https://procontract.due-north.com/Opportunities/Index); (d) Express an interest; (e) Download the tender documents (from the ProContract Activity summary screen). Any questions or clarifications relating to this tender opportunity should be submitted to ESPO as a message on the eProcurement Portal, once an Expression of interest has been completed. Lot 1: Electronic Document Scanning and Software. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to-end scanning solution including preparation, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents. To include the supply, implementation and maintenance of EDRM (Electronic Document & Records Management Software), associated Project management and training. Lot 2: Document Storage and Retrieval Services. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide preparation, collection, storage, retrieval and the secure disposal of documents plus any associated services. Lot 3: Total Document Management Solution. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to end solution for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated training. Suppliers will also be required to provide a consultancy Service designed to scope and shape a full document management solution to help customers manage all their documents. Lot 4: Enhanced Handling and Security Requirements. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide enhanced safe and secure document management solutions for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes secure handling of documents, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated and training. Lot 5: Confidential On-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide on-site confidential shredding services. Lot 6: Confidential Off-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide off-site confidential shredding services. Lot 7: On-Site and Off-Site High Security Shredding to NPSA Standards. This Lot requires suppliers to provide high security shredding services to NPSA standards.

We would like to hear from organisations who have experience of conducting research with health, local authority and VCS services, to support the development of a gambling needs assessment. The levy provides increased, independent and sustainable funding for the research, prevention and treatment of gambling-related harms across Great Britain. We would like feedback from providers who have experience in conducting research with VCS and statutory organisations and services. We are keen to hear from VCSEs, SMEs and those based in Worcestershire. Lot 1: .

Das bestehende Infoportal bildet derzeit das zentrale Data-Warehouse- und Berichtssystem der WIBank. Es konsolidiert Daten aus verschiedenen Quellsystemen und stellt darauf basierende Berichte sowie Meldungen für Förderprogramme der Europäischen Union, des Bundes und des Landes Hessen bereit. Gegenstand des Projekts ist die Bereitstellung einer neuen Reporting-Plattform für die Fachbereiche Finanz- und Rechnungswesen, Risikomanagement und Treasury. Hierzu zählen insbesondere die Anbindung von SAP WIBank als initialem operativen Quellsystem, der Aufbau des Data Marts „Meldewesen“, die Übernahme historischer Daten aus dem bestehenden Infoportal sowie die Umsetzung der definierten Zielberichte. Nach Abschluss des Projekts wird die entwickelte Plattform im Rahmen einer kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung ausgebaut. Dies umfasst insbesondere die Anbindung weiterer Quellsysteme, den Aufbau zusätzlicher Data Marts sowie die Migration weiterer Berichte aus dem bestehenden Infoportal. Langfristig soll das bestehende Infoportal vollständig abgelöst und außer Betrieb genommen werden. Sämtliche Leistungen sind auf Grundlage einer Rahmenvereinbarung und mithin erst auf gesonderten Abruf/Einzelauftrag hin zu erbringen. Die Obergrenze für Abrufe aus dem Rahmenvertrag beträgt insgesamt EUR 6,5 Mio. (brutto). Für die weiteren Einzelheiten wird auf die Anlage I 02 - Anlage 0_Leistungsbeschreibung verwiesen.

signals.buyer_name: Bundesrepublik Deutschland, vertreten durch das Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soziales, dieses vertreten durch die Präsidentin der Bundesanstalt für Arbeitsschutz und Arbeitsmedizin
signals.description: Beschaffung forschungsbasierter Leistungen im Projekt "Digital Smart Regulations" für den Arbeitsschutz - Entwicklung und Erprobung von Ansätzen für den Einsatz digitalisierter Vorschriften und Regeln im Arbeitsschutz Lot LOT-0001: Beschaffung von forschungsbasierten Leistungen im Projekt "Digital Smart Regulations" für den Arbeitsschutz. Ausgangspunkt des Vorhabens: Für die Erarbeitung, Bereitstellung und Anwendung Technischer Regeln im Bereich des Arbeitsschutzes sind digitale Lösungen sinnvoll. Das gilt sowohl für die Regelsetzung in den Arbeitsschutzausschüssen beim Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soziales (siehe https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), als auch für die Bekanntmachung der Regeln durch das BMAS und deren Anwendung in den Betrieben sowie für Beratung und Vollzug. Im Bereich der Normung liegt von der Initiative Digitale Standards von DIN und DKE (IDiS) das Konzept "Digital Smart Standards" vor (siehe https://www.dke.de/idis ). Dieses wurde in einem vorangegangenen Forschungsprojekt F 2542 der BAuA exemplarisch angewendet (siehe https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 und Projektwebseite https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). Eine Methodik für die schrittweise Erarbeitung von maschinenlesbaren und maschinenausführbaren Prüfregeln wurde daraus abgeleitet (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Ansätze für die Transformation von Technischen Regeln für Arbeitsstätten in digitale Regeln. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Auftragsgegenstand und Ziele: Ausgehend von den vorliegenden Ansätzen und Erkenntnissen ist in einer Studie zu untersuchen, inwieweit Ansätze für "Digital Smart Standards" auf weitere Bereiche des Vorschriften- und Regelwerks zum Arbeitsschutz übertragen werden können und die in den Arbeitsschutzausschüssen erarbeiteten Arbeitsschutzregeln zu "Digital Smart Regulations", also in das Level 2 "Maschinenlesbares Dokument" überführt sowie zukünftig für die Level 3 "Maschinenlesbare und ausführbare Inhalte" und Level 4 "Maschinenlesbare und interpretierbare Inhalte", weiterentwickelt werden können. Diese Studie ist Gegenstand der vom Auftragnehmer zu erbringenden Leistungen. Ziel sind Handlungsempfehlungen für die weitere Digitalisierung von Arbeitsschutzvorschriften und -regeln in Deutschland. In maßgeblichen fachlichen Anwendungskontexten und Anwendungsfällen, die in Zusammenarbeit mit den Arbeitsschutzausschüssen beim BMAS auszuwählen sind, sind die Prozesse von der Erstellung über das Management und die Bereitstellung bis zur betrieblichen Anwendung von Regeln sowie die Umsetzungsmöglichkeiten zu betrachten. Anforderungen aus Arbeitsschutzvorschriften und -regeln sind in der Praxis insbesondere bei der Gefährdungsbeurteilung durch Arbeitgeber zu berücksichtigen. Im Projekt ist daher durch den Auftragnehmer zu untersuchen, wie die Inhalte der Arbeitsschutzregeln in exemplarischen digitalen Umsetzungen der Prozesse der Gefährdungsbeurteilung sowie in ggf. vorhandenen Datenmodellen angewendet und mit weiteren Anforderungen koordiniert werden können. Der Auftragnehmer führt die Ergebnisse systematisch zusammen, wertet sie aus und leitet darauf aufbauend konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen ab. Das Projekt trägt dazu bei, das jeweilige Regelwerk auf Nutzerseite zukünftig übersichtlicher und leichter digital anwendbar zu machen sowie die Prozesse der Erstellung, Weiterentwicklung, Verwaltung und Bereitstellung der Regeln effizienter zu gestalten.

signals.description: Shropshire Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to understand the current market for digital solutions that support unpaid carers. This engagement will help inform the Council’s future commissioning approach before any decision is made about whether to tender, use an existing compliant route, develop an alternative model, or take no further procurement action. Shropshire Council has an established Unpaid Carer Support offer. Recently this has become an all-age offer supporting Young Carers and Parent Carers. The Unpaid Carers portal will be an online offer which will be available to Unpaid Carers 24/7 throughout the journey of their caring role. We are aware there are a large proportion of people who do not identify as an Unpaid Carer, we envisage the portal will support with that identification and will provide relevant up to date information to support families in a preventative manner. Any proposed solution should offer the following support: Increase the identification recognition and early interventions for unpaid Carers Delay and reduce the need to access high-cost statutory provision Improve accessibility to information, advice and guidance, improve links and signposting to services that are already available nationally, regionally and locally. Support Unpaid Carers to access self-help and self-management support to reduce the need for Unpaid Carers crisis interventions. Include access to Unpaid Carers 'self-assessment' focused on individualised outcomes The solution should have the capacity to collect and produce relative data regarding demographics, ethnicity, age range as well as information such as when and where the portal is accessed. signals.description: Das Projekt richtet sich an potenzielle internationale Reisengäste und beschreibt die Möglichkeit von Aktivreisen in Deutschland (Fokus auf Wandern, Radfahren, ggf. Kanu).Die Experience präsentiert nicht einzelne Destinationen oder touristische Produkte, sondern vermittelt die charakteristischen Qualitäten Deutschlands als vielfältiges Aktivreiseziel. Im Mittelpunkt stehen typische Reiseerlebnisse und die Kombination aus Natur, Bewegung, Kultur, Genuss und Regeneration, die den Aktivurlaub in Deutschland auszeichnen. Das Projekt dient nicht nur der Wissensvermittlung, sondern der Gast soll an gesprochen, „an die Hand genommen“ werden, leichte Aufgaben erledigen und emotional eingebunden werden. Dies hat mindestens den gleichen Stellenwert wie die Information. Ziel: Verlängerung der Verweildauer. Das Projekt soll für die Ausgabekanäle Virtual Reality (inkl. Inflight Entertainment in Flugzeugen mit VR-Brillen), Mobile und Web entwickelt werden, um eine möglichst hohe Reichweite zu generieren.In diesem Pilotprojekt geht es um eine neue Art des Destinationsmarketings, bei dem Kombinationen der Nutzeransprache, Nutzerführung und Contentdar stellung aus Gaming, VR, künstlicher (KI-gestützter) Contentgenerierung und realem Content kombiniert werden. Der Bieter muss diese verschiedenen Skills vereinen und ein ansprechendes, interaktives Produkt erstellen, dass den Kunden vom Reiseland Deutschland fasziniert. Neben virtuellen Umgebungen, Szenerien und Avataren (bzw. digitalen Wesen/Objekten) soll das Projekt auch bestehende Medien der DZT (Fotos, Filme, Drohnenaufnahmen, 360-Grad-Panoramen etc.) beinhalten und diese in beeindruckender Form, interaktiv präsentieren. In Abhängigkeit vom Konzept müssen ggf. noch weitere Medien digital erstellt, gekauft oder geshootet werden. Zudem ist erstmalig der Einsatz von (wenigen) Gaussian Splats vorgesehen, sofern inhaltlich und technisch sinnvoll. Der geplante Mix aus (z.T. fotorealistisch) digital erstelltem Content und echten Bildern, Panoramen und Videos sowie Avataren ist im Tourismusmarketing nach unserer Kenntnis bisher einzigartig. Weitere Informationen entnehmen Sie bitte aus der Leistungsbeschreibung im Angebotsvordruck. Lot LOT-0000: Active travel in Germany. signals.description: Carmarthenshire County Council is undertaking an Early Market Engagement exercise to better understand the care rostering, scheduling and workforce management solutions currently available within the market. The Council currently utilises a rostering and scheduling solution across its Residential and Domiciliary Care Services and wishes to engage with suppliers to understand available products, functionality, market developments and delivery models that may support future service requirements. signals.description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food. Lot 1: . None

signals.description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.

Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-4-improving-efficiency-and-patient-experience-in-nhs-transport

signals.description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.

signals.description: Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia kokonaisuudesta, johon sisältyvät: 1. kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaille 2. hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu 3. hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä edellä mainitun palvelun tuottamiseen hyvinvointialueen omana toimintana. Hankinnassa turvalaitteilla tarkoitetaan erilaisia kotiin annettavia turvalaitteita, joilla voidaan parantaa kotona asuvan asiakkaan turvallisuutta. Hankittavia turvalaitteita ovat turvapuhelimet ja niiden lisälaitteet, paikantava turvaranneke sekä ratkaisu yhteisöllisen asumisen ovivalvontaan. Hälytysten vastaanottopalvelulla tarkoitetaan palvelua, jossa otetaan vastaan turvalaitteiden kautta tulevat hälytykset, tehdään alustavan arvion avuntarpeesta ja välitetään pyyntö edelleen turva-auttajille. Palvelun tulee toiminnassa vuorokauden ympäri vuoden jokaisena päivä. Hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmällä tarkoitetaan järjestelmää, jolla tilaaja voi ottaa eri turvalaitteiden hälytykset vastaan ja edelleenvälittää ne tehtävänä turva-auttajille. Lapin hyvinvointialueella on tarkoitus ottaa hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu omaksi toiminnaksi alustavan aikataulun mukaan keväällä 2028. Hyvinvointialue hankkii hälytysten vastaanottopalvelua siihen asti, kunnes vastaanottojärjestelmä on otettu käyttöön, minkä jälkeen vastaanottopalvelun hankinta päättyy. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Kilpailutuksessa valitaan yksi toimitta puitesopimustoimittajaksi. Puitejärjestelyn kautta hyvinvointialue hankkii valitulta toimittajalta turvalaitteita ja palveluita sopimuskauden aikana tarpeen mukaan. Hyvinvointialueen tarpeet voivat vaihdella sopimuskauden aikana, eikä tarjouspyynnöllä sitouduta tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Puitesopimuksen sopimuskausi on määräaikaisena kaksi vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimus jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. Hankintayksikön tarkoitus on tehdä sopimus valitun toimittajan kanssa heti, kun tarjousaika on päättynyt, tarjoukset on vertailtu, hankintapäätös on tehty ja muutoksenhakuaika on päättynyt. Hankintayksikön arvion mukaan ajankohta on lokakuun 2026 aikana. Laitevaihtojen toteutuksen ja muiden käyttöönottoon liittyvien toimien aikataulut sovitaan yhdessä valitun toimittajan kanssa molempien osapuolten tarpeet huomioivalla tavalla. Lisäksi valitulta toimittajalta hankitaan hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä kokonaisuutena, johon sisältyy järjestelmän toimittaminen ja sen jatkuva palvelu. Järjestelmän jatkuvan palvelun sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska kyseessä on yhtenäinen tavaroiden ja palveluiden muodostama kokonaisuus, jonka kaikkien osasten yhteensopivuus on voitava varmistaa. Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaiden turvallisuuden kannalta on tärkeää, että yksi toimittaja vastaa koko kokonaisuuden toimivuudesta. Hankintailmoitus on julkaistu toisen kerran uudelleen, koska kaksi aiempaa hankintamenettelyä on täytynyt keskeyttää hankinta-asiakirjojen muutostarpeiden vuoksi.

signals.description: The aim of the procurement is to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of equipment, consumables and production services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør. East. The procurement shall support the implementation and use of uniform physical and digital identification of locations and equipment based on international GS1 standards. Locations shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GLN and the equipment shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GIAI, in the form of GS1 Digital Link and other standardised GS1 syntaxes. Through the use of international standards, marks shall be able to be used by digital systems in Helse Sør-Øst, e.g. systems for Facility Management (FM)/property management, clinical logistics, medical engineering, ERP, etc. The procurement shall result in: - Standardised types of brands for locations and equipment. - Support for multiple information carriers on brands - Support for local production of brands - Support for production of large volumes of brands as external services. - Standardised production basis. - Secure management of business critical information. The procurement includes systems for both local production of brands in the health companies, and production of large volumes of brands. The system for local production can include production equipment, necessary software and/or integration components, consumables, equipment for encoding/programming NFC and UHF RFID, training, support, maintenance and documentation. The contracting authority will, together with the chosen supplier, establish a set of standardised brand types that will be used for the production of labels for locations and equipment. A tag type is a documented specification that specifies how a brand should be designed and produced.

Edellä mainittujen palveluiden lisäksi osana palvelukokonaisuutta palveluntuottaja toimittaa tilaajan käyttöön palvelutuotannon edellyttämät, täysin tuotantokäytössä olevat tietojärjestelmät SaaS-palveluna (järjestelmäkokonaisuus) tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. signals.description: This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others. Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises. This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A. Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender. All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually. This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts. Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender. Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT. If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed. The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website. We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells. The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives. Our needs are specific and will vary. We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required: Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use; Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project. Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells. Lot 1: Bridges Supply, Repair and Maintenance. The Authority supplies, installs and maintains bridges on public rights of way throughout the National Park including bridleways and footpaths for use by horse riders, cyclists, mobility scooters and pedestrians. We are seeking suppliers who can assist with the following: • Supply bridge materials as component parts and/or complete structures in a variety of materials including recycled plastic, metal, timber, concrete, stone. These bridges will need to be to our specification or bespoke design in some cases. • Using the materials listed above, build and install those bridges in a wide variety of locations, including some remote and difficult to get to. This can include machine work, working with helicopter delivery companies, working with hand tools, demolition and construction of abutments. • To repair existing bridge structures in situ, including replacement of handrails, decking boards, beams, abutments e.g. stonework. • To provide designs to structural engineers' standards to meet the supplied specifications for a wide range of bridge types, including footbridges, bridleway bridges and those suitable for road traffic in some instances. This might include reviewing and revising our existing designs and specifications, to producing bespoke designs for individual unique locations and bridge types. • For structural engineers to inspect the current condition of bridges and abutments to check they meet the standards for the required user groups and to sign off newly installed bridges to verify that they meet the required specification and standards. • To provide, erect and use scaffolding, including in remote locations, to complex designs, to enable the team to carry out maintenance and construction work on the bridges and other rights of way work in a safe and secure manner, following current industry and health and safety standards. Services required: • Supply of prefabricated bridge kits • Provision of materials e.g. timber/ plastic/ metal • Bespoke design of bridges • Installation of bridges • Repair of bridges • Engineer surveys on bridges • Scaffolding on bridges to support safe installation or repair Lot 2: Supply of Materials. The Authority requires qualified suppliers for the supply, delivery and installation of materials and services to support our countryside construction and maintenance projects. It aims to ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective delivery of materials and services while complying with health, safety, and environmental standards. It also aims to facilitate the provision of locally sourced materials to reduce transport mileage, to support the economic wellbeing of the National Park, and to showcase local products. Suppliers under this framework must demonstrate relevant experience, proven quality standards and the capacity to meet delivery schedules. Services and materials will be provided according to defined specifications, with monitoring of performance through key indicators such as timeliness, quality, and responsiveness. Suppliers must ensure that all materials supplied meet relevant British Standards or industry-recognised equivalents. Goods required: • Pipes/drains • Grass seed • Treated and some graded timber for fencing and the construction of timber boardwalks • Gates • Waymark roundels for Public Footpaths, Bridleways, Byways and permitted routes • Local stone (from the Lake District) for construction of unbound surface paths, stone for drainage works and dry-stone walling and bridge revetments • Plastic boardwalks from 1m to 3m width with non-slip finish • Metalwork (gate springs, gate hinges, catches screws, nuts, etc.) • Screened (inert) topsoil • Fingerposts and Waymarkers • Benches • Fencing wire • Metal fencing (i.e. Clipex) • Native tree species grown from seeds sourced in seed zone 301, or if unavailable, 302. Lot 3: Minor Practical works under £50,000. The Authority requires a range of qualified suppliers for delivery of practical works and services supporting our countryside access and nature conservation projects across the National Park. This often requires working in remote locations with challenging access. All work standards and specifications will be set out in relevant documents. All work will need to be carried out to all relevant legislative requirements by appropriately trained and qualified staff. Examples of the types of work the Authority requires are: construction, repair and maintenance of structures, furniture and surfaces forming part of Public Rights of Way work (PROW) such as footpaths, bridleways and byways. Surfacing -The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Un-bound, bound, crushed stone or tarmac paths. • Machine construction of profile inversion (subsoil) paths • Supply and delivery and laying of stone flags • Construction and repair of pitched stone paths using local stone. Drainage works - The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Plastic drainage of all sizes. • Stone culverts • Drainage ditches. Fencing, Walling and hedgerows- The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • All forms of fencing including Post and rail, post and wire, metal estate style • Drystone and bound (mortared) walling in local vernacular style. • Hedgerows planted and maintained in the local vernacular style. Vegetation management • Mechanical and chemical control of vegetation on public rights of way, open land and formal sites including control of Invasive Non-Native Species (INNS). Countryside Furniture - The supply, construction, repair, and maintenance of; • Wooden and metal fingerposts, signs, benches, gates stiles, boardwalks and other countryside furniture. Tree Works • Surveying, planting, felling, maintaining and high access rope work relating to tree management. • Supply of native tree and plant species. Transportation • Transportation of plant, machinery, materials to accessible parts of the National Park. Habitat Restoration Works • Restore peatland areas by hand and or machine. • Planting of native species Traffic Management Supply and management of traffic control systems on public highways up to 'A' road standards. Please see our Rights of Way Specification Resource Pack at Appendix 1. Services required: • Surfacing • Drainage installation and maintenance • Sub soiling • Installation of stone flags • Pitching to create paths • Fencing • Walling • Vegetation control and clearance • Installation of countryside furniture (e.g. fingerposts/benches) • Tree works • Planting (trees and hedgerows) • Spraying (herbicides) • Hedge trimming • Salting and gritting paths • Trail sweeping • Mooring works (Ullswater/servicing) • Graffiti removal • Woodland management through thinning, coppicing, halo thinning, girdling, and processing of timber • Bracken management through mowing, rolling, or chemical application • Scrub management • Hedge laying • Grassland restoration and management activities; mowing, baling, weed wiping, harrowing, seeding, plug planting • Chemical control of invasive, non-native species Please also see Appendix 1 of the ITT. Lot 4: Consultancy and Specialist Services. The Authority requires a range of consultancy services to assist it in carrying out its statutory duties and project work. Our work is incredibly varied, and consultancy is required in relation to all stages of a project from feasibility, design, planning, and surveying. We require specialist advice in relation to Rights of Way, and lake/water works. Other areas of the Authority's work include historic buildings and environment, planning and architectural surveying so we welcome consultants from a range of specialist practice areas. Advice sought could be, for example, in the form of written reports, design drawings to agreed standards, survey datasets (in agreed formats) or overseeing the delivery of defined projects around nature recovery or access and recreation related works. This Lot is divided into three individual sub-lots based on the type of consultancy required. Lot 4a: Access and Recreation services required: • Traffic management e.g. traffic lights • Planning consultancy • Structural engineering design • Construction Design and Management works • Electronic counting surveys - people, horses, vehicles, bikes etc • Rights of Way consultants • Project managers • Visitor monitoring and data • Property management and consulting Lot 4b: Natural Environment: • Ecological surveys (e.g. habitat surveys using NVC, UKHAB frameworks/Habitat condition monitoring using BNG or CSM methods/specialist surveys for taxonomical groups i.e Bryophytes, Lichens, protected species groups, insects) • Baseline surveys • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat Management and Monitoring Plans • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat bank monitoring survey and reporting • Habitat and property management and monitoring planning • Drone Surveys • Geospatial surveys Lot 4c: Historic Environment: • Historic Structure Surveys (e.g. condition surveys, archaeological and structural assessments and repair schedules) • Archaeological surverys (e.g condition surveys, fieldwork, heritage assessments) • Contract administration services for Historic Structure Construction Projects Lot 5: Training and Development. he Authority requires qualified companies to provide essential training to ensure that individuals working in various roles are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to work safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements and legislation. The training requirements cover a range of topics, including first aid, manual handling, chainsaw, plant and equipment operation (to name a few - please see Appendix 2 for a full concise list), which are required to minimise risks and ensure a safe working environment. Courses will need to be accredited by recognised bodies, providing learners with the necessary qualifications to meet industry standards. • First aid • Manual handling • Practical countryside management training e.g.: walling, fencing • Plant and machinery operations e.g.: 4WD training, chainsaws, quad bikes, strimmers; • Species management training (e.g tree conditions surveys) • Please see Appendix 2 of the ITT for a list of all training requirements. Lot 6: Supply and repairs of Equipment, Plant and Machinery. The Authority has an internal fleet of various machinery, equipment and plant. We require services for maintenance and servicing of all types of equipment, plant, and machinery. We also require suppliers who can source and provide new equipment, plant and machinery as required. For example, current categories include: • Plant: diggers, dumpers, tracked power barrows, remote flails, chippers. • Vehicles: land rovers, pick-ups, 4x4s, electric vans and cars. • Power tools: compressors, jet washes, cement mixers, drills, stone saws, angle grinders chop saws etc. • Hand tools: spades, panel saws, shovelers, tampers, steel bars etc. • PPE: chainsaw trousers, hard hats, eye protection, hearing protection etc. • Fuel (Aspen, diesel, petrol, LPG etc.) • Servicing and safety inspections (e.g. LOLA checks on lifting strops and chains, and general servicing of tools like compressors) • Bi-annual service of outboard motors for patrol boats • Servicing of patrol boat trailers • Annual servicing of life jackets, patrol boat radar systems and CCTV systems. We require maintenance and servicing of all machinery and vehicles. Services required: • Servicing • Repairs • Maintenance (boats, outboard engines, trailers, lifejackets, diggers, dumpers, radar, CAT scanners, generator calibration) • Inspection of kit/ equipment • LOLER items checks • Supply of new machinery as required Lot 7: Helicopter Operations. Provide helicopter operations for the transportation of stone and other materials to remote locations throughout the Lake District: movement of prebagged fell stone in one-ton bags to high altitude worksites on popular mountain paths. Stropping, bunding and prepping materials such as flagstones, fence posts or bridge materials prior to flying. Providing specialist safety advice to officers involved in helicopter operations - before during and after any operations. Provide experienced ground crew for hooking on and assessing loads, receiving loads where necessary and ensuring specialist kit or equipment such as signage strops and radio headsets are available. To provide an indication of volume, in 2025 LDNPA flew over 400 tonnes of stone to high altitude sites. Suppliers must hold all relevant Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approvals, USL Licensing and operate in accordance with UK aviation regulations. Services required: • Transport of materials and equipment within the Lake District National Park using helicopters • Airlift operations • Load preparation (stropping, bunding) • Ground crew provision • Flight planning and risk assessment Lot 8: Higher Value Practical Works - £50,000 and over. The Authority secures frequent bids for grant money provided by national, regional and local government as well as charitable organisations and private funding organisations. This funding enables the Authority to undertake larger scale and usually multi-facetted projects or programmes of work varying in value from the high tens of thousands of pounds to the low millions of pounds. Such projects may involve delivery of one type of product or service across a range of sites throughout the park or a multi-facetted project including access, nature conservation, interpretation, and conservation of the heritage-built environment. We are looking for suppliers who can provide work at scale and across a range of areas, either directly or by acting as Primary Contractors and providing project management and delivering work through co-ordinating multiple suppliers and contractors. Examples of such work packages include the establishment of the Coast-to-Coast National Trail, barn restoration through the Farming in Protected Landscapes programme and Access for All projects. The type of work is similar to that contained in Lots 1, 2, and 3 but at large scale. Services required: • General construction project work (see description) • Sub soiling • Stone flags • Pitching • Construction Design and Management work • Supply and construction of bridges • Public path works • Securing relevant consents, assents and planning permissions • Woodland Management • Grassland restoration • Riverbank Stabilization

signals.description: Ards and North Down Borough Council is currently preparing to initiate a procurement process to appoint an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down. The Holywood Innovation Hub is a project funded through investment from the Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) and Ards and North Down Borough Council. It will focus on micro and small businesses within the digital, creative and screen industries: providing facilities and a secure environment to meet specific security, connectivity and technical needs. The proposed hub is intended to provide accommodation for the creative technology sector, specifically for start-up and smaller firms seeking to grow within the sector. It would also seek to provide accommodation for larger established 'anchor' tenants and potentially act as a short-term flexible base for FDI projects supported by NI Screen. The proposed hub is also intended to create an ecosystem within the creative technology sector: improving skills and employability across Ards and North Down and the overall Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) region. A primary reason for market failure in this sector is stated as a lack of suitable accommodation. This project will address this situation, supporting the growth of firms in the digital creative sector beyond the initial 'work from home' phase. The capital funding requirement for the proposal is £8,921,200 from the BRCD, with a further contribution of £1.1m from Ards and North Down Borough Council (ANDBC), further funding is required from the private sector to unlock this funding. ANDBC intends to appoint an operator for the Innovation Hub at an early stage of project development. The operator will assume management responsibilities and associated risks as set out in the final contractual structure. The operator will be appointed prior to the procurement of the Integrated Consultancy Team (ICT) responsible for the design of the Innovation Hub, enabling operational requirements and commercial considerations to be incorporated into the design and helping to maximise the hub's long-term economic performance. Prior to initiating the procurement, the Council is undertaking an Expression of Interest (EoI) and Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Exercise . This EoI/PME exercise is being conducted pursuant to section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023 for the purposes of: (a) developing the Council's requirements and approach to the procurement; (b) designing conditions of participation and award criteria; (c) preparing the tender notice and associated tender documents; and (d) identifying suppliers capable of performing the proposed contract. The pre-market engagement is intended to facilitate high-level conversations to identify potential interested suppliers and capabilities to inform the Council's procurement approach. A summary of the opportunity is detailed in the brochure and questionnaire documents that can be accessed via the CfT documents area (Resource ID 6717503) on the eTendersNI platform (https://etendersni.gov.uk).
